sections.COMMENTS:
An E-W contraction belt runs from the Sicily Channel to the Eolian Islands, about 50 km off the northern Sicily coast. This belt is thought to accommodate 2-5 mm/y of the total Africa-Europe convergence (Dâ€™Agostino and Selvaggi, 2004; Serpelloni et al., 2007).
In the past 30 years several events with M>5 originated in this area, including the Mw 5.9 Palermo earthquake of 2002. They are mostly shallow compressional earthquakes with NNW-SSE P-axes (Goes et al., 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2004; Vannucci et al., 2004). This contraction trend is consistent with the plate motion vectors derived from GPS data. Some moderate-size historical earthquakes, located inland along the northern coast of Sicily, likely belong to this seismic belt (e.g. Guidoboni et al., 2003; Jenny et al., 2006).
Recent interpretations of seismic profiles in this area hypothesized reactivation of previous north-dipping thrust structures inherited from the building phase of the Sicily-Maghrebian chain (Africa northern margin; Pepe et al., 2005; Cuffaro et al., 2011). One of these is thought to be the source of the Mw 5.9, Palermo earthquake of 6 September 2002 (Cuffaro et al., 2011). However, available data are not enough to rule out the existence also of south-dipping active structures (Doglioni et al., 2007; Billi et al., 2007, 2011; Cuffaro et al., 2011).
We propose that this Source coincides with the hypothesized north-dipping plane. Strike and dip were taken from mapped structures and fault plane solutions. The rake was taken parallel to the plate motion vectors derived from GPS data and P-axes of focal mechanisms. Slip rate values are estimated considering the geodynamic and tectonic setting.
